meta.title: Hungarian A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hungarian → English (see the Hungarian, recall the meaning) and English → Hungarian (see an English meaning, recall the Hungarian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words of Hungarian for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Hungarian has examinations at these levels, but no graded word list for any of them was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 454 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs and study, clothes, more food and cooking, the rooms and furniture of a home, the town and its services, travel and holidays, nature, the seasons and the compass, animals, health and the body, feelings and character, free time and sport, telling what happened when, the higher numbers and measures, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing, cooking and doing — and the other 296 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hungarian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Hungarian dictionaries give them, in the third person singular (eszik "eats", lát "sees"), the form the endings are built on. The 381 nouns show their plural, their accusative and their "his, her" form, the part vowel harmony makes hard to guess (ló, lovak, lovat, lova), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 154 verbs show their "I" form, their past and their infinitive (eszik, eszem, evett, enni), and behind the fold the present in both conjugations — the definite one is used when the object is definite (látok egy házat, "I see a house"; látom a házat, "I see the house") — the past, the conditional and the imperative by person. The Hungarian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 748 of the 750 words, three apiece for 743 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

Azért fizetnek hetente, hogy az igazi véleményemet ne írjam le az újságba, amelyikkel kapcsolatban állok. A többiek hasonlóan vannak fizetve ilyen dolgokért, és ha bárki közületek lenne olyan őrült, hogy az őszinte meglátásait írná le, kint találná magát az utcán másik állás után nézve. Ha én megengedném magamnak, hogy a legőszintébb meglátásaim megjelenjenek a lapom egyik számában, huszonnégy órán belül nem lenne munkám. Az újságírók munkája, hogy lerombolják az igazságot, hogy nyíltan meghazudtolják, elferdítsék, becsméreljék azt Mammon lábainál csúszva, és hogy eladják az országukat és fajtájukat a napi betevőért. Te is tudod, én is tudom, ezért mi ez a baromság a független sajtó ünneplésével? Paprika Jancsik vagyunk, akiket zsinórokon rángatnak. There is no such thing, at this stage of the world’s history in America, as an independent press. You know it and I know it. There is not one of you who dare write your honest opinions, and if you did, you know beforehand that it would never appear in print. I am paid weekly for keeping my honest opinions out of the paper I am connected with. Others of you are paid similar salaries for similar things, and any of you who would be foolish as to write honest opinions would be out on the streets looking for another job. If I allowed my honest opinions to appear in one issue of my papers, before twenty-four hours my occupation would be gone. The business of the journalist is to destroy the truth, to lie outright, to pervert, to vilify, to fawn at the feet of Mammon, and to sell his country and his race for his daily bread. You know it and I know it, and what folly is this toasting an independent press? We are the jumping jacks, they pull the strings and we dance. Our talents, our possibilities and our lives are all the property of other men. We are intellectual prostitutes.
